To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the equation of state (EOS) for dense QCD is very sensitive to the renormalisation scale, and that this leads to large uncertainties in the mass-radius relation of quark stars, which are the densest objects in the universe.

1) the mass-radius relation of quark stars is strongly affected by the equation of state; 2) the equation of state is strongly affected by perturbative QED effects, which are not yet included in our calculations; 3) the equation of states of the perturbative and hard dense loop approaches are very similar, which is a consequence of the fact that they are both based on a perturbative expansion of the quark self energy.
(i) The quark mass dependence of the quark star radius is weak and the quark star masses are almost independent of quark mass.
